now the print generator uses the table of contents from the stub instead of using it from the python code.

This removes the need for a very dodgy hardcoded value containing the number of pages in the table of contents (typically 1 or 2). This way, this hardcoded value does no longer to be adjusted for each piece, as the table of contents is read from the stub. The code that reads the table of contents from the stub is very very messy (lots of reverse engineering to figure out how pdf stores its data), it will be cleaned very soon.

improvement : made pymusco cope with any pdf, regardless the format of
its contents.

pymusco is now simpler : instead of attempting to dig into the pdf to
find the scanned image (which failed when the scanned image was split
into multiple images by the scanner), pymusco now simply extracts each
page as a pdf file.

As a result, pymusco is now simpler and more robust, but there are
identified drawbacks:
1. pymusco now doesn't handle properly the pages in landcape modes (and
we do have some sometimes; eg : the speech of a musical piece is in
landcape mode and the scanner detected it and put the scanned page in
landcape mode accordingly)
2. this extraction method is no longer suited for image processing odf
the scan to improve it (eg convert gray to black/white), but these
processings have not yet been implemented anyway...

hopefully fix to issue 1

added a function that checks the integrity of a pdf file. This helped me
to discover that the corruption seems to be caused by
subprocess.check_call, which seems to not wait for the completion of the
command before carrying on, as should be expected.

I replaced subprocess.check_call with subprocess.Popen + wait(), which
seems to work better. For security, I added a call to detect malformed
pdf in the case this fix doesn't prove to work 100%.
